content.thinking:
I'm checking the claims one at a time. The first, that some io-shop requests failed with errors, is backed by what a reader saw. For the duration claim, the record says the incident still wasn't back to normal at 13 seconds, so I'll support it with the "how long it lasted" line. The third claim, about the business cost being the failed customer requests, is where I'm still working through the wording.

I'm weighing the third claim against the record. The record says failed requests weren't counted and no loss was estimated, and it doesn't say who sent the requests, so tying the business cost to failed customer requests goes beyond what's there. I'll flag that one. The rest check out: the cause is unknown, no on-call responder was paged since no incident was linked, and nothing was done to end the incident.

flags.quote: The cost to the business was those failed requests from customers who were trying to use io-shop.
rows: not counted by the metrics - requests failed
No loss was estimated: no onset was measured to count it from.
flags.why: The record estimated no loss and did not count failed requests, and it never says who sent the failing requests, so it gives no cost to the business and does not mention customers.

supported.quote: Some requests to io-shop failed with errors
rows: What a reader saw: io-shop requests failed with errors
How long it lasted: at least 13s {duration}
Why, in plain words: The cause is not known.

supported.quote: No on-call responder was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: Nothing was done to end the incident.
rows: What was done to end it: Nothing was done to end it.
